newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRs-FOCUS-Qantas sees more profit pressure.
newsitem.headline: RTRs-FOCUS-Qantas sees more profit pressure.

text.p: Australian flag carrier Qantas Airways Ltd said on Wednesday higher jetfuel prices and a strong Australian dollar had had a negative impact on profitability, but it still expected to boost returns this financial year.

Qantas, which is 25-percent owned by British Airways Plc, has run into turbulence in its second year as a publicly-listed company and soft aviation market conditions have forced the airline to cut costs to meet its profit expectations.

"In terms of trading so far this year, we have seen a softening in the market against our expectations at the time our budgets were set," chairman Gary Pemberton told shareholders at the annual meeting.
"In addition, the high fuel costs and the high Australian dollar will have a negative impact on our 1996/97 profitability," Pemberton said.

The cautious outlook was further bad news for shareholders, who are already upset with the carrier's poor share price performance. Qantas shares have spent most of the month hovering around the A$1.90 (US$1.50) issue price for small investors.

Institutional investors paid A$2.00 per Qantas shares at the time of the airline's float in July 1995. Qantas shares have also been one the worse performers amongst the top 100 companies on the local bourse over the past year.
The Qantas board gave the shareholders little comfort during the 2-1/2-hour meeting. Pemberton said: "...we are still looking to improve on last year's profit."
"This prediction is not without downside risk and the extent of any improvement will be largely determined by market conditions in the second half of the year," he added.
Qantas announced a 37-percent rise in 1995/96 net profit to A$246.2 million in August and at the time said it expected 1996/97 profits to be around the A$260-A$270 million level.

The Australian national carrier, like many airlines around the world, is looking at cutting costs to improve profitability and raised its existing target of A$330 million in cost cuts for 1996/97 by a further A$100 million.
The cuts would be across the board at all levels of the airline's expenditure, Pemberton said.
Qantas also unveiled plans for A$280 million in additional spending on terminal improvements and expected additional product development expenditure to exceed A$430 million over the next three years.
Qantas shares closed steady at A$1.96, down from a record high of A$2.47 hit on March 4 but are their all-time low of A$1.79 hit earlier this month.
